why: The baseline: sequence, choice and parallel in one small log.
A redo loop (e, f) around a parallel part.
Two independent choices around a shared activity.
The first choice decides the last one: not free-choice, which the alpha-algorithm cannot express.
b repeats on the spot; the alpha-algorithm warns and the miners need a self-loop.
b, d, b: a loop of length two, the case of the Heuristics Miner's second rule.
Both kinds of short loop on the same activity (issue 73).
The first activity can be skipped or repeated.
a and c never occur without each other: one optional stretch, not two (Leemans 2017, p. 233).
A sequence cut must hold for every pair across it, not for some pair.
Cases with no events at all.
Empty traces are exactly 20 % of the log: the boundary of IMf at 0.2 (issue 74).
One case in 51 swaps b and c: rare behaviour of the kind the noise threshold is for.
The rare order is exactly 20 % of the frequent one: the boundary of the noise filter.
One case in 81 does d early: the noise threshold changes the model.
One case runs backwards (d, a): without the threshold the whole model turns parallel.
The same, around two optional activities.
b and c in both orders, and a case that stops early.
No cut exists: the result depends on the order of the fall-throughs.
a, b repeats before c.
a is both the start and the end activity.
The smallest log.
A single activity, one to three times.
Every order of b, c and d.
A parallel pair that can be done again.
z is not in the model: counted by token replay since 0.16.2, a log move in an alignment.
Nothing in the trace is in the model.
b is left out in some cases: a model move.
b and c the other way round against a strictly sequential model.
b twice where the model allows it once.
The case ends before the model does: tokens remain.
An empty case on a model that needs two steps.
